la:verb:discedo.html:
dis-cēdo, cessi, cessum, 3 (
perf. sync. discesti, ), v. n.
(With the notion of dis predominating.)
To part asunder, divide, separate (rare but class.; cf.: linquo, relinquo, desero, desum, destituo, deficio).
Lit.: cum terra discessisset magnis quibusdam imbribus,: caelum,opens,; , i. e. clears off, (this last is quoted in ): sulcus vomere,: VT SODALITATES DECVRIATIQVE DISCEDERENT, SC. ap. ; cf.: cum discedere populum jussissent tribuni,: populus ex contione,: armati in latitudinem, Sisenn. ap. : in duas partes,: in partes,; cf.: in manipulos,: fumus in auras,: ad semina rerum,: palus multos discessit in amnes,: citius paterer caput hoc discedere collo,.—
Trop.: divisio in tres partes,: haec in duo genera,.—
To part from one's connection with one, i. e. to leave, forsake, desert (rare but class.).—With a or ab: uxor a Dolabella discessit, Cael. ap. : ab amicis in re publica peccantibus,: ab amicis,: a nobis,: milites in itinere ab eo discedunt,: a Perseo,.
(With the notion of cedere predominating.) To depart from any place or person, to go away from, to leave (cf.: proficiscor, abeo; so most frequently in all periods and sorts of composition).
Lit.
In gen.: constr. with ab, ex, or absol., rarely with de—With ab: cum discesti ab

hero, atque abisti ad forum, ; so with abire,; : quod legati eorum paulo ante a Caesare discesserant,: ab suis,: ab exercitu,; et saep.: a senis latere numquam,: a vallo,: ab loco,: a litore,fin. et saep.—With ex: non modo illum e Gallia non discessisse, sed ne a Mutina quidem recessisse,: ex contione,: e medio,: e patria, et saep.—With de: de foro,; ; : de colloquio,.—With abl. without a prep.: templo,: finibus Ausoniae,: lecto,: Tarracone,: Capua,.—Absol.: ille discessit, ego somno solutus sum,; so,; ; et saep.—Pass. impers.: ne longius ab agmine discedi pateretur,: ab concilio disceditur,fin.: de colloquio discessum,; ; —

Designating the term. ad quem, to go away to any place: in silvas,: ex fuga in civitates,fin.: in castra,: in proximos colles,: in loca occulta,: ad urbem, et saep.: Capreas,: ex castris domum,; cf. simply domum,; : domos suas,: cubitum,.—
In partic.
In milit. lang., to march off, march away, decamp: discessit a Brundisio obsessionemque nostrorum omisit,: ab Gergovia,: a mari Dyrrhachioque,: ab Zama,: ex ea parte vici,: ex hibernis,: ex eo loco,; cf.: ex iis locis cum classe,fin.: Tarracone, et saep.: dispersi ac dissipati discedunt,; so absol., fin.; 6, 33, 4 et saep.; so milit.: discedere ab signis,to quit the standard, leave the order of battle,; ; : qui discedere et abire cœptabant,i. e. to break ranks and go away,; cf.: ab ordinibus signisque : ab armis,to lay down one's arms,; ; ; ; —
Also in milit. lang., to get away, come away, come off in any manner from the battle (victorious, conquered, wounded, etc.); and sometimes to be translated simply to become, to be, etc.: superiores,; so, superior,: victor,; cf.: victor ab hoste,: victus,to be conquered,: graviter vulneratus, et saep.: aequo proelio,; cf.: aequa manu,: aequo Marte cum Volscis,: sine detrimento, et saep.—Pass. impers.: a proelio disceditur,.—
Transf. beyond the milit. sphere (freq. into the judicial sphere, on account of its analogy to the former): ut spoliis Sexti Roscii hoc judicio ornati auctique discedant,: superiorem,; so, liberatus,: omnium judicio probatus,: impunita (tanta injuria), et saep.: discessisses non male,; cf.: pulchre et probe et praeter spem,: aut cum summa gloria aut sine molestia,; cf.: a judicio capitis maximā gloriā,: ita tum discedo ab illo, ut qui se filiam Neget daturum,; cf.: si possum discedere, ne causa optima in senatu pereat,
Trop.
In gen., to depart, deviate, swerve from; to leave, forsake, give up: nihil a statu naturae, nihil a dignitate sapientis,: a fide justitiaque,: longe ab consuetudine mea et cautione ac diligentia,: a constantia atque a mente, atque a se ipse,; cf.: a se,; ; ; : a recta conscientia, Att. ap. : a sua sententia,: ab officio, : ab oppugnatione castrorum, et saep.: a judiciisque causisque,: a litteris,: ab illa acerrima contentione,: ab illa cavillatione,: a suscepta semel persuasione, et saep.—
In partic.
Pregn., to pass away, to vanish, to cease (very rarely): modo audivi, quartanam a te discessisse,had left you,: ex animo memoria alicujus,: hostibus spes potiundi oppidi discessit (opp. studium propugnandi accessit), : ubi hae sollicitudines discessere,—
In alicujus sententiam, in polit. lang., to pass or go over to another's opinion, ; ; ; cf. the opp., in alia omnia, (v. alius). In like manner: decurritur ad illud extremum atque ultimum SC., quo nisi paene in ipso urbis incendio ... numquam ante discessum est,which had never before been resorted to,; so perh.: ex oratione Caesaris ... hanc in opinionem discessi, ut, etc.,—
Ab aliquo, in Cicero's letters in the sense of to leave out of consideration, i. e. to except: cum a vobis meae salutis auctoribus discesserim, neminem esse, cujus officiis me tam esse devinctum confitear,if I except you, you excepted,: ut cum ab illo discesserint, me habeant proximum,: amoris erga me, cum a fraterno amore domesticoque discessi, tibi primas defero,.!*? Once in the part. perf.: custodibus discessis, Cael. ap. P.

la:verb:disputo.html:
dis-pŭto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
Orig. in mercant. lang., to cast or reckon up, to calculate a sum by going over its items; to estimate, compute: ubi disputata est ratio cum argentario,.—
Transf. beyond the mercant. sphere, to weigh, examine, investigate, treat of, discuss a doubtful subject, either by meditating or (more commonly) by speaking upon it (good prose; very freq. in Cicero's philos. and rhet. writings; cf. for syn.: dissero, discepto); constr. usual. with accus. of neutr. pron. or with de and abl. (cf. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 372): in meo corde eam rem volutavi et diu disputavi,: ea, quae disputavi, disserere malui quam judicare,: neque haec in eam sententiam disputo, ut, etc.,: aliquid pro tribunali multis verbis,: hoc, et saep.: (Druides) multa de sideribus atque eorum motu, etc.... disputant,: de moribus, de virtutibus, de re publica,: de omni re in contrarias partes,: cf. ; ; : ab his, qui contra disputant,; cf. : non inscite ad ea disputat, quae, etc.,; cf. ; : quale sit de quo disputabitur,: disputatur in consilio a Petreio et Afranio, et saep.: nunc utriusque disceptator eccum adest, age disputa,i. e. relate, tell,; cf. : rem alicui,i. e. to state, represent,.—With acc. and inf.: isti in eo disputant, Contaminari non decere fabulas,i. e. maintain, Ruhnk.—
In late Lat.
To discuss, preach: in synagoga,; ; .—
To dispute, contend in words: quis eorum major esset,: cum diabolo,.

With acc.: nihil fingam, nihil dissimulem, nihil obtegam,: aliquid (with tegere),; with obtegere,; with celare,; with occultare,; ; cf. : nec, ut emat melius, nec ut vendat, quicquam simulabit aut dissimulabit vir bonus,; cf. la:verb:disco.html:
disco, dĭdĭci, 3 (
part. fut.: sic disciturum, etc., App. ap. P.), v. a.
from the root da-, Gr. δεδαώς, δαῆναι; dak-, cf. doceo, doctus, Gr. διδάσκω
, to learn, to learn to know, to become acquainted with, etc. (for syn. cf.: capio, percipio, concipio, comprehendo, intellego, cognosco, nosco, agnosco, animadverto, calleo, scio—very freq. in all periods and sorts of writing).
With acc.: litteras Graecas senex didici,; : so, litteras,: jus civile,; : litteras apud aliquem,: dialectica ab aliquo,: artem ab aliquo, et saep.: aliquid de aliquo,: virtutem ex me, fortunam ex aliis,; cf. : fabularum similia,: artes,: palaestram,: affectum,: inde vocabula prima,: elementa prima,: dulces querelas,; cf. preces, et saep.: me peritus Discet Iber,; cf.: quem (Augustum) didicere Vindelici,: omnes crimine ab uno, et saep.—Pass.: dum est, unde jus civile discatur,; cf. jus,: Crassus, quod disci potuit de jure didicit,: tot artibus discendis, et saep.—
With inf. or acc. and inf.: pueri qui nare discunt,: rapere et clepere, (ap. ): Latine loqui,: nobis ignoscere,: assem in partes diducere,: bene ferre magnam fortunam, et saep.: bene ubi quod consilium discimus accidisse, etc.,: discit, Litavicum ad sollicitandos Haeduos profectum,: animadverti et didici ex tuis litteris te omnibus in rebus habuisse rationem, ut, etc.,; : deos didici securum agere aevum, et saep.—
With relat. clause: plures discent, quemadmodum haec fiant, quam quemadmodum his resistatur,: quantum in Etruria belli esset,: patriae quid debeat, etc., et saep.—
Absol.: disces tu quidem a principe hujus aetatis philosophorum, et disces quamdiu voles,: didicit,i. e. oratory,; ; : discendi aut visendi causa maria transmittere,; so, discendi causa,; ; al.: se ita a patribus majoribusque suis didicisse, ut, etc.,. —Ellipt.: discebant fidibus antiqui, sc. canere, (cf.: docere fidibus,: scire fidibus,).—
Transf., of inanimate subjects: manus,: nec varios discet mentiri lana colores,: arbores, prooem.—
To teach = docere (late Lat., cf. μανθάνειν, and Eng. learn): falsa discentes,.

la:noun:discrimen.html:
discrīmen, ĭnis, n.
contr. from discerimen à discerno; cf. crimen from cerno
, lit.,
that which separates or divides two things from each other (for syn. cf.: differentia, discrepantia, diversitas, distantia); hence,
Lit., an intervening space, interval, distance, division, separation: cum (duo maria) pertenui discrimine separarentur,: minimum quos inter et hostem Discrimen murus clausaque porta facit,: aequo discrimine,; : parvum leti,; : dare discrimina costis,i. e. to separate them,: quae (sc. littera F) inter discrimina dentium efflanda est,: agminum,: ungulae,: comae,; and in like manner poet.: telluris pectitae, i. e. furrow, Col. Poët. 10, 94; : medium luci,.—Hence, med. t. t., the dividing membrane, the midriff, diaphragm, ; —
Trop. (so most frequent).
In gen., a distinction, difference: amabat omnes, nam discrimen non facit, Lucil. ap. : iste, qui omnia jura pretio exaequasset omniumque rerum delectum atque discrimen pecunia sustulisset,; cf.: officia tollebantur delectu omni et discrimine remoto,: sit hoc discrimen inter gratiosos cives atque fortes, ut illi, etc.,: sine ullo sexus discrimine,; cf.: rapti per agros viatores sine discrimine liberi servique,: omisso sui alicuique discrimine,: divinarum humanarumque rerum,: recti pravique,: vocum,; cf. so of the different tones of the strings: septem discrimina vocum, et saep.—Poet.: tenues parvi discriminis umbrae,i. e. of easy gradation,. —
In partic.
With respect to disputed matters, which are to be distinguished between, and thus decided upon, the decisive point, turning-point, critical moment, determination, decision: quoniam res in id discrimen adducta est, utrum ille poenas rei publicae luat, an nos serviamus,to this point,; cf.: ea res nunc in discrimine versatur, utrum ... an, etc.,; : vicit disciplina militaris, vicit imperii majestas, quae in discrimine fuerunt, an ulla post hanc diem essent,: haec et his similia haud in magno equidem ponam discrimine, shall not regard as of great moment, id. praef. § 8: postquam adesse discrimen ultimum belli animadvertit,: instant enim (adversarii) et saepe discrimen omne committunt,abandon the most decisive points, et saep.—Poet.: experiar, deus hic, discrimine aperto, An sit mortalis,the test,.—
Transf., a dangerous, decisive moment, crisis, dangerous condition; risk, danger, hazard: in ipso discrimine periculi aliquem destituere,; so, periculi,: in summo rem esse discrimine, * ; cf.: adducta est res in maximum periculum et extremum pene discrimen,: salus sociorum summum in periculum ac discrimen vocatur,: in extremo discrimine ac dimicatione fortunae,: in veteris fortunae discrimen adducitur,; cf.: aliquem in discrimen capitis adducere,; so, capitis,: si ei subito sit allatum periculum discrimenque patriae,: rem publicam in discrimen committere,; ; cf.: fuitque dies illa tenebrarum et discriminis,.

discī^plīna (also uncontr. DISCIPVLINA, Num. Hadr. ap. Eckh. D. N. V. 6, p. 503; the Cod. palimps. , prima manu has likewise DISCIPVLINA: so,
discipulina, Lorenz; Fleck.; cf. Ussing ad loc.), ae. f.

la:verb:dissolvo.html:
dis-solvo, solvi, sŏlūtum, 3, v. a.,
to loosen asunder, to unloose, disunite, separate, dissolve, destroy (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: facilius est apta dissolvere quam dissipata conectere,: opus ipsa suum eadem quae coagmentavit natura dissolvit,: dissolvunt nodos omnes et vincla relaxant,: contextum,: stamina,: ornatus comae,: capillum,: sparta navium,: pontem, et saep.: nubila ventis,; cf. nubes (ventus, with diducit),: glaciem (sol),to melt,: aes (fulmen),: corpora (vis),: se (venti vortex),: tenebras luce, Müll.: dissolutum navigium vel potius dissipatum,; so, navem,; : stomachum,i. e. to loosen, relax,: ilia sua visu,: resinam omnem oleo,: collegia, : cohortem Germanorum, et saep.: animam,i. e. to die,; cf. ; .—
In partic.
In mercant. lang., to pay, discharge what one owes: dinumerando solvere: aes alienum praediis venditis,; ; : nomen,: omne quod debuit,: quae debeo,: pecuniam pro iis rebus, * : pecuniam publicam ulli civitati,: poenam,to pay a fine,; cf.: dissolvere et compensare damna,: vota,; .—*
Mid., transf. to the person: quarum (possessionum) amore adducti dissolvi nullo modo possunt, free or release themselves from debt, .—
In medic. lang., like digerere, discutere, to discuss, dissipate morbid matter, ; ;
Trop., to dissolve, abolish, abrogate, annul, destroy.
In gen.: utilitas si amicitias conglutinaret, eadem commutata dissolveret,; cf. : amicitiam,: societatem,: consortionem,: matrimonia, et saep.: perjurium,; cf. religiones,: acta Caesaris,; cf.: leges Caesaris,: judicia publica,: hoc interdictum, et saep.: argentariam,: regiam potestatem,; cf. rem publicam,: severitatem,: frigus, et saep.: mortem cuncta mortalium mala dissolvere,; cf. with pers. object: plerosque senectus dissolvit,.—
In partic.
In rhet. and philos. lang., to refute, reply to, answer an assertion: criminatio tota dissoluta est (with diluere),: seu proposita confirmamus, seu contra dicta dissolvimus,; ; ; ; —

Trop., of quality, to differ, be different=differre, discrepare (freq.): ut distare aliquid aut ex aliqua parte differre videatur,; cf.: quia res differebant, nomina rerum distare voluerunt,: moribus et legibus distant (civitates),; cf. : in totum metaphora brevior est similitudo, eoque distat, quod, etc.,: multum inter se distant istae facultates longeque sunt diversae atque sejunctae,: multum inter se genera dicendi,; : hominum vita tantum distat a victu et cultu bestiarum,; so with ab, ; ; ; ; ; ; cf.: quid enim tam distans quam a severitate comitas?. —With dat.: infido scurrae distabit amicus,; so, paulum sepultae inertiae celata virtus,: quid aera lupinis,: pulchra et exactis minimum distantia,: enthymema syllogismo,— Impers.: distat, there is a difference: distat, sumasne pudenter An rapias,; ; ; .

la:verb:dispergo.html:
di-spergo, in late Lat. and sometimes in MSS. of the older authors written di-spargo (cf. aspergo and conspergo), si, sum, 3,
v. a., to scatter on all sides, to scatter about, disperse (freq. and class., esp. in the part. perf.).
Lit.: per agros passim dispergit corpus,; cf. per hypallagen: membrorum collectio dispersa (coupled with dissipare), (but in , the right reading is: dispessis membris, not dispersis, v. dispando): cur (deus) tam multa pestifera terra marique disperserit?: nubes dispergunt venti,: an tibi jam mavis cerebrum dispergam hic?; for which: ut cerebro dispergat viam, besprinkle, : caprae dispergunt se, contra oves so congregant et condensant in locum unum,; cf.: comites dispersi,; so the mid.: dispersi, of persons,; ; and esp. freq. of soldiers,; ; ; et saep.; , et saep.; cf.: dispersi a suis pars cedere, etc.,; and in the verb. fin. act.: quae (duo milia evocatorum) tota acie disperserat,had distributed,: fimum,: vitem traducibus dispergere atque disrarare,: lactuca dispergitur, set out, i. e. planted, : color dispergitur omnis, (not disperditur, v. Lachm. ad h. l.): ubi brachia et crura inaequaliter dispergit,i. e. moves at random,: Mesopotamia vicatim dispersa,i. e. divided,: magna pars Judaeae vicis dispergitur, et saep.—Poet.: aries dispergit saxa (with effundere muros), Cort.: dispersa capillos,: quo latior (res) est, in cunctas undique partis Plura modo dispargit et ab se corpora mittit,; so with in and acc., ; ; : tripartitum exercitum plures in manus,: aër dispargitur ad partis minutas corporis,.
Trop.: in praesentia tantummodo numeros et modos et partes argumentandi confuse et permixte dispersimus: post descripte ... ex hac copia digeremus,; cf. ; ; : bellum tam longe lateque dispersum,: in re dispersa atque infinita,: plebis vis soluta atque dispersa in multitudine,: rumorem,: falsos rumores,; and with acc. and inf.: volgus fingendi avidum disperserat accitum in adoptionem,had given out,: membratim oportebit partis rei gestae dispergere in causam,: vitam in auras,; cf.: partem voti in auras,.— Hence, adv. in two forms:
dispersē, dispersedly, here and there (very rare): disperse et diffuse dictae res,: multis in locis dicta,. —
dispersim, ; ; .

la:verb:discerno.gloss: to separate, set apart, divide, part
senses: to separate, set apart, divide, part
la:verb:discerno.html:
dis-cerno, crēvi, crētum, 3,
v. a., to separate, set apart.
Lit., to separate, part, divide (freq. since the Aug. per.): equas, ne inter se pugnare possint,: ordines (preceded by senatus a populo secretus), : lignum a carnibus,: Lusitaniam a Baetica,: neque mons erat, qui fines eorum discerneret,i. e. to mark out, determine,; cf. poet.: (saxum) telas auro,to interweave with gold,; : haec ipsa fortuna huc illucve discernit,divides, distributes,.—In the part. perf., divided, separated: duae urbes, magno inter se spatio discretae,; cf.: Peraea a ceteris Judaeis Jordane amne,: Philippus mari tantum Ionio discretus,; so, sol tanto intervallo,: uxor velo,: ager saxo,: decurias pluribus nominibus, et saep.— Of the hair, parted: discretaque collo Caesaries,: divisa discretaque tellus,divided and separated,: tellus (opp. permixta),: ubi discretas insula rumpit aquas,: sedes piorum,set apart, retired,: quae cum sint turpissima discreta ac separata, turpius junguntur,: septem discretus in ostia Nilus, (for which: septem digestum in cornua Nilum, ); cf. .
Trop.
To separate things according to their different qualities, to distinguish between, discern (freq. and class.): alba et atra,: discernere et dispicere insidiatorem et petitum insidiis,: jus et injuriam,: probanda atque improbanda,: fas atque nefas, et saep.: id quod visum erit a falso,: pantheras a pardis solo candore, et saep.: verba discerni articulatim,: suos, * : piceam visu,: temperantiam duobus modis, et saep.: animus discernit, quid sit ejusdem generis, quid alterius,: pecuniae an famae minus parceret haud facile dis cerneres,; so with an, ; ; ; cf.: nec discernatur, jussu injussu imperatoris pugnent,

—

To determine, settle: limes agro positus litem ut discerneret arvis,: discerne causam meam,.—
To except, omit, .—Hence, *
discernen-ter, adv., with a distinction, , no. 81.—
discrētim, adv., separately, distinctly, : singillatim ac discretim,: adoriri,: tradi,; Hilar. in Psa. 138, 23.

la:verb:dispono.html:
dis-pōno, pŏsŭi, pŏsĭtum (contr. dispostum, ; ), 3,
v. a., to place here and there, to set in different places, to distribute regularly, to dispose, arrange (cf. dispenso, II.—freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen., to set in order, arrange, dispose: libros confusos antea,, a; cf.: Homeri libros,: oculos (harundinum),; cf. brassicam,: arbores,: quidque suo loco,; cf.: pennas in ordine,; for which: disjecta membra in ordinem,: obliquos ordines in quincuncem,: aciem,; : male capillos,; cf. comas,; : tectos enses per herbam,: ceras per atria,; for which: expressi cera voltus singulis disponebantur armariis,: tabernas deversorias per litora et ripas,: cubicula plurifariam, et saep.—Poet.: (Prometheus) corpora disponens, etc., qs. arranging the parts, limbs,i. e. fashioning, forming, (4, 4, 9 M.): moenia versu,i. e. to describe,; cf. .—
In partic., milit. t. t., to set in order, arrange, to draw up, array a body of men, a guard, military engines, etc.: praesidia disponit, castella communit,; so, praesidia,: stationes,; : custodias,: cohortes,: equites,; : exploratores,: insidias,; : equos,to station in relays,: ballistas machinasque, et saep.: custodias in muro,; : expeditos, et saep.; cf.: legiones in Apulia hibernorum causa,: tormenta in muris,: sudes in opere, et saep.: milites iis operibus quae, etc.,: exploratores omni fluminis parte,: classem omni ora maritima,: naves in litore pluribus locis separatim,: cohortes castris praesidio, et saep.: praesidia custodiasque ad ripas Ligeris,; cf. ; : praesidia cis Rhenum,; cf.: legiones Narbone circumque ea loca hiemandi causa,: equites per oram maritimam,; cf. ; ; et saep.
Trop.: verba ita disponunt ut pictores varietatem colorum, paria paribus referunt,; so of the regular arrangement of the parts of a discourse,; ; ; et saep.; cf. also : fac ut plane iis omnibus, quos devinctos tenes, descriptum ac dispositum suum cuique munus sit,; cf. ministeria principatus in equites Romanos,: imperii curas,: consilia in omnem fortunam ita disposita habebat (the fig. being borrowed from milit. lang.),: in disponendo die,in arranging the business of the day,: diem,; ; ; cf. otium,: tempus otiosum,: opus et requiem pariter, et saep.—
In post-class. lang., with acc. and inf. or rel. clause, like the Gr. διατάσσω, to settle, determine: non alienum erit disponi, apud quem puer interim educetur,: Thebani apparere paucos disposuerunt, (dub.): excursatores quingentos sensim praeire disposuit,; .—With ut, .—Hence, dispŏsĭtus, a, um, P. a., regularly distributed; hence properly ordered, arranged (very rare): studia ad honorem disposita,: vita hominum,; also transf.: vir dispositus,an orderly speaker,.—As subst.: lumina ex disposito relucentia,.—Comp.: dispositius, praef. fin.; cf. med.—Sup. Boëth. Cons. Phil. 4, pros. 2.—Adv.: dispŏsĭte, orderly, methodically: accusare istum,: dicere,: exponere, § 18: mundus effectus est (with ordinate),.— Sup.: aedificare,.

la:verb:dissilio.html:
dis-sĭlĭo, ŭi, 4, v. n.
salio
,
to leap or burst asunder, to fly apart.
Lit. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): duo de concursu corpora lata si cita dissiliant,; cf. ; : dissiliunt ferventi saxa vapore,; so, silex igni,; cf.: mucro ictu dissiluit,: aera (sc. frigore),: uva pressa pede,: haec loca vi quondam et vasta convolsa ruina Dissiluisse ferunt,; : omne solum,: lamina,; 12, 488 al.: boves degustatā bupresti, burst open, = dirumpere, ; : risu,: (vox) ubi Dissiluit semel in multas,has broken up into many, (preceded by: partis in cunctas dividitur vox).—
To leap: in Jordanem,.—
Trop.: gratia fratrum geminorum dissiluit,was dissolved,.

la:noun:dispendium.html:
dispendĭum, ii, n.
dispendo
(opp compendium, v. 3, dis, II.),
expense, cost, loss (mostly ante- and post-class.; cf.: impensa, impendium, sumptus; also: noxa, damnum, detrimentum, jactura, incommodum).
Lit.: dispendium ideo, quod in dispendendo solet minus fieri, Müll.: sine damno et dispendio,; cf. so with sumptus,: minore nusquam bene fui dispendio,: ut gratiam ineat sine suo dispendio,: neque dispendi facit hilum, Enn. ap. Müll.; cf. * : alicui afferre dispendium,: quod dispendium pauci intellegunt,: dispendia (comae),; cf. : viarum,i. e. a roundabout way,: silvae,.—
Trop.: hic tibi ne qua morae fuerint dispendia tanti, loss of time, * : famae,: disciplinae,.

la:verb:discurro.gloss: to run about, in different directions, or to and fro; to roam, wander
senses: to run about, in different directions, or to and fro; to roam, wander
la:verb:discurro.html:
dis-curro, curri and cucurri (
perf. discucurri, ; ; : discurrisse,; oftener curri,; ; ; ), cursum, 3, v. n.
To run different ways, to run to and fro, run about (not freq. till after the Aug. per.; in Cic not at all): in muris armata civitas, * : deus in montibus altis,: plebs pileata tota Urbe,: circa deum delubra,; cf.: circa vias,: per omnes silvas,; cf.: per ambitum lacus,; and: per Baianum sinum equis,: more victorum cum palma discucurrit, et saep.—Designating

the term. ad quem: ad portas,; : ad arma,: ad praedam,: ad officia,: ad rapiendas virgines, et saep.: in latera,; cf.: a media in utramque partem,.—Pass. impers.: ilicet in muros tota discurritur urbe,: in tribus ad suffragium ferendum,: ab caede ad diripiendam urbem,— In the pass., with a homogeneous subject: discursis magnis itineribus,.—

Of inanimate and abstract subjects: discurrentes maculae in gemma,; : catenae circa latera,: (Nilus) diversa ruens septem discurrit in ora,; : fama tota urbe discurrit,: mens discurret utroque,.—
Transf., to traverse, run through or over, hasten through (post-class.): latius arva,: Gallias,: tramite aliquo discurso,: discursis itineribus magnis,.—
Trop., like Gr. διελθεῖν, to speak at length of a thing, to discourse of (post-class.): super quo nunc pauca discurram, (cf. in this sense the Romance discorrere, discourir, and v. 2, discursus, II.).

la:adj:discolor.html:
dis-cŏlor, ōris (abl. -ori, ; —post-class. form of the
fem. discolora, in the signif. of II. A.: lana, Prud. στεφ. 10, 302: serta, ed. Mai.: venustas,; and once discoloria vestis,), adj., of another color, not of the same color (opp. concolor).
Lit.
With dat.: neutra pars esse debet discolor lanae (shortly before: si palatum atque lingua concolor lanae est),: (vestis) sumatur fatis discolor alba meis,: aura auri,.—
Absol., party-colored, of different colors: habere arculas, ubi discolores sint cerae,: signa, * : miles (black and white in the game of draughts), Jahn; cf. agmen (in running a race),.—
Transf.
Party-colored, variegated: aves,: vestis,: arma,—
In gen., of various kinds, different, various: matrona meretrici dispar erit atque Discolor, * : amnis pelago,: rerum discolor usus,.

la:verb:dispicio.html:
di-spĭcĭo, spexi, spectum, 3, v. n. and a.
, to see through all parts (cf. Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 236 and 237), to see with an effort, to open wide the eyes in order to see, to look through, to see; to glance, to gaze; and actively, to descry, discern, perceive (class.; esp. freq. in Cic. Lachm. l. l. prefers dispicere in many passages where the best editions have despicere, e. g. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf. Conington ad ; Munroad N. cr.).
Lit.
Neutr.: isti autem tantis effusis tenebris ne scintillam quidem ullam ad dispiciendum reliquerunt,; cf.: tanta oborta caligo est ut dispicere non posset,; : catuli, qui jam dispecturi sunt, caeci aeque et hi, qui modo nati,: ut primum dispexit,: ad terram aspice et dispice, Oculis investigans astute augura,.—
Act.: nubila, Lachm.: longe cunctas in partis,: dispecta est et Thule,: ut nequit ullam dispicere oculus rem,.—
Transf., to investigate, make an examination: dispicientibus consistorianis et militaribus,.—
Trop., to perceive mentally, discern, discover (commonly as act.): si imbecilli animi verum dispicere non possint,; cf. : mentem principis,: merita,: in ea re Pompeius quid velit, non dispicio,: sine jam aliquid dispiciam,to find out,; cf. .—
Meton. (mostly in the imperat.), to consider, think, reflect upon: nunc velim dispicias res Romanas,: discerne et dispice insidiatorem et petitum insidiis,; pr.: dispice, an tu, etc.,: dispice, ne sit, etc.,: prius dispiciamus de his, quae, etc.,; cf. ; and absol.: virtus est, ubi occasio admonet, dispicere,.
la:verb:dispicio.inflection: spexi, spectum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:verb:dissideo.gloss: to sit apart; to be divided, separate or remote from
senses: to sit apart; to be divided, separate or remote from
to be unlike, different or dissimilar; differ, disagree
la:verb:dissideo.html:
dis-sĭdĕo, ēdi, essum, 2, v. n.
sedeo
,
to sit apart, to be remote from, to be divided, separated.
Lit. (only poet. and very rare): quantum Hypanis dissidet Eridano,: sceptris nostris, *: ab omni dissidet turba procul Laïus,; .—Far more freq. and class.,
Trop., to be at variance, to disagree, to think differently. —Constr. with ab, cum, inter se, or absol.
With ab: nullam esse gentem tam dissidentem a populo Romano odio quodam atque discidio,; cf. ; : a senatu,: a tribuno plebis (consules),: a Pompeio in tantis rebus,: a nobis (altera pars senatus), et saep.: non verbis Stoicos a Peripateticis, sed universa re et tota sententia dissidere,; cf. : animus a se ipse dissidens secumque discordans,: Archytas iracundiam, videlicet dissidentem a ratione, seditionem quandam animi vere dicebat,; cf. : ab ingenio matris, et saep.—
With inter se: leviter inter se dissident,: cupiditates in animis inclusae inter se dissident atque discordant,; cf. —
With cum: cum Cleanthe, doctore suo, quam multis rebus Chrysippus dissidet,; cf.: non cum homine, sed cum causa,.—*
With dat.: virtus dissidens plebi,.—(ε) With abl. manner: ex quo facile intellectu est verbis eos, non re dissidere,: capitali odio,.—(ζ) Absol.: de qua (definitione summi boni) qui dissident, de omni vitae ratione dissident,; (opp. congruae): cum Julia primo concorditer et amore mutuo vixit, mox dissedit,he fell out with her,: Medus dissidet armis,; cf.: dissidet miles,: dissident olores et aquilae,live at enmity, et saep.: spes incesserat dissidere hostem in Arminium ac Segestem,i. e. were divided into two factions, that of Arminius and Segestes,.—Pass. impers.: histriones, propter quos dissidebatur,.—
Of inanimate and abstract subjects in gen., to be unlike, dissimilar, different, various; to differ, disagree.
With a: nostra non multum a Peripateticis dissidentia,; cf.: scriptum a sententia, : gestus a voce,—
With cum: voluntas scriptoris cum scripto,: verba cum sententia scriptoris,—
Absol.: si inaequalitate dissident (supercilia),: supercilia dissidentia (opp. constricta),; cf.: si toga dissidet impar,i. e. sits uneven, one-sided, (cf. the opp. aequaliter sedet, ): si duo haec verba idem significant, neque ulla re aliqua dissident,.

la:verb:distraho.gloss: to draw, pull or drag asunder; tear in pieces, separate forcibly, divide; scatter
senses: to draw, pull or drag asunder; tear in pieces, separate forcibly, divide; scatter
to sell separately (in parcels), retail; sell (in general)
to draw in different directions; divide, distract, perplex
to separate in sentiment, estrange, alienate
la:verb:distraho.html:
dis-trăho, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.
To pull asunder, tear in pieces, to separate forcibly, divide (freq. and class.).
Lit.
In gen.: corpus quod dirimi distrahive non possit,; cf. : exanimor, feror, differor, distrahor, diripior,; Pentheum diripuisse aiunt Bacchas; nugas ... prae quo pacto ego divorsus distrahor,; cf.: Mettum Fufetium equis ad curriculum ex utraque parte deligatum distraxit, Varr. ap. ; so of the same: corpus passim,; of Hippolytus: turbatis distractus equis,: quae (materia) neque perrumpi neque distrahi potest,; cf. vallum (with diripere),: ut aciem ejus distrahi paterentur,i. e. to be separated, broken up,: Taurus mons mediam distrahens Asiam, et saep.—
In partic., in mercant. lang., to sell separately, in parcels, to retail = divendere (mostly post-Aug.): dividant, differant, dissipent, distrahant, Lucil. ap. : coëmendo quaedam tantum ut pluris postea distraheret,: agros,; cf. fundum,: merces,: bona venum, et saep.—
In gen., to sell: instrumentum,: levi pretio aetatulam,—
To waste, squander: apsenti hic tua res distrahitur tibi,. —
Trop., to draw in different directions; to divide, distract, perplex: qui haec natura cohaerentia opinione distraxissent,; cf. : distrahitur in deliberando animus,; cf., shortly before: in quo considerando saepe animi in contrarias sententias distrahuntur; cf.: distrahor, tum hoc mihi probabilius, tum illud videtur,: cum Tiberium anceps cura distraheret, vine militum ... an, etc.,; cf. : obsessos hinc fides, inde egestas inter decus ac flagitium distrahebant,: oratoris industriam in plura studia distrahere nolim,: sic distrahuntur in contrarias partes impotentium cupiditates,; cf. : res publica

distracta lacerataque, ; cf. quae sententia omnem societatem distrahit civitatis,: Caesarem et Pompeium perfidia hominum distractos in pristinam concordiam reducere, Balbus ap. A.: amorem,: concilium Boeotorum,: collegia,: matrimonium, et saep.: rem,to frustrate, prevent,: controversias, i. e. dirimere,to end, adjust,; : voces, i. e. to leave a hiatus (opp. contrahere), : qua ipse fama distraheretur, i. q. differretur (cf. differo, B. 2.),would be assailed,.

To tear away, draw away, part, to separate, remove.
Lit.: membra divellere ac distrahere,: illam a me distrahit necessitas,; ; .—
Trop.: sapientiam, temperantiam, fortitudinem copulatas esse docui cum voluptate, ut ab ea nullo modo nec divelli nec distrahi possint,.—
Of persons, to separate in sentiment, to estrange, alienate: aliquem ab aliquo (preceded by: a conjunctione avocare, and: a familiaritate disjungere),; so with divellere,.—Hence, distractus, a, um, P. a.
Divided (very rarely): (conjectus animaï) divisior inter se ac distractior,.—
Trop., distracted, perplexed: distractissimus tantorum onerum mole,.—Adv. does not occur.

la:verb:dissulto.gloss: to leap apart, fly in pieces, burst apart
senses: to leap apart, fly in pieces, burst apart
la:verb:dissulto.html:
dissulto, āre,
v. freq. n. [dissilio], to leap apart, to fly in pieces, burst asunder (poet., and in post-Aug. prose): dissultant ripae,: tanti crepitus,: ferrum utrimque,: Vulcanius ardor,: aquae splendor, darts here and there with tremulous motion, cf. .

la:adj:dissimilis.html:
dis-sĭmĭlis, e, adj.,
unlike, dissimilar, different (as the opp. of similis and consimilis, v. 3. dis, II.; cf.: dispar, impar, absimilis; very freq. and class.).—Constr. with the gen., dat., with atque, et, inter se, or absol. (for this variety in the construction, cf. esp. to 83 med.).
With gen.: (P. Crassus) dum Cyri et Alexandri similis esse voluit, et L. Crassi et multorum Crassorum inventus est dissimillimus,fin.. alicujus dissimilis in tribunatu reliquaque omni vita, ; so, Scetani,: artificium hoc ceterorum,: offensio odii,fin.: cives tui,; cf. sui,; ; ; ; cf. also under
.—
With dat.: nihil tam dissimile quam Cotta Sulpicio,: quis homini,: illa contentio huic judicio,: hoc superiori,: proximo,: tam fortibus ausis,: hoc illi,.—
With atque or et, ; cf.: aut quiescendum, quod est non dissimile atque ire in Solonium aut Antium; aut, etc.,; and: haec consilia non sunt dissimilia, ac si quis aegro, etc.,: dissimilis est militum causa et tua,; ; .—
With inter se: dissimiles longe inter se variosque colores,; ; ; sq.; ; cf.: cum inter vos in dicendo dissimillimi sitis,; and in a twofold construction: qui sunt et inter se dissimiles et aliorum,.—(ε) Absol.: dissimillimi motus,: voces,: eos, qui nascuntur eodem tempore, posse in dissimiles incidere naturas propter caeli dissimilitudinem, et saep.: hac in re multum dissimiles,: quid sit in quoque dissimile,: pro dissimillimo,—(ζ) With in and acc.: aetate et forma, haud dissimili in dominum erat, to his master, i. e. so as to pass for his master, .—(η) With ab: dissimilis valde ab omnibus,.—Hence, dissĭmĭlĭter, adv., differently, in a different manner (rarely): efficere voluptates,; ; —With dat.: haud dissimiliter navibus sine gubernaculo vagis,.

la:verb:discerpo.gloss: to pluck or tear to pieces; to rend, mutilate or mangle
senses: to pluck or tear to pieces; to rend, mutilate or mangle
la:verb:discerpo.html:
dis-cerpo, psi, ptum, 3, v. a.
carpo
,
to pluck or tear in pieces, to rend, to mangle (class.).
Lit.: animus nec secerni nec dividi nec discerpi nec distrahi potest,; cf. : inter orgia Bacchi discerptum iuvenem sparsere per agros,: aliquem,; : semiustum cadaver (canes),: membra gruis, et saep.: in parvas partīs aurum,; —

la:verb:discordo.html:
discordo, āre, v. n.
id.
,
to be at variance, to differ, to quarrel (rare but class.).
Lit.: discordare inter se,: cupiditates in animis dissident atque discordant,: animus a se ipse dissidens secumque discordans,: cum Cheruscis,: adversus ventrem (membra),.—

dissensus, ūs, m.
dissentio
